subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that live as a shared approval/elevated policy instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source and release checks show the requested mode is absent, but deciding when a chat identity may skip approval prompts changes a security boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

options.title: Keep Existing Approval Model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators wanting no prompts must use the existing full/off exec approval policy with the host approvals file configured accordingly.

options.title: Add Telegram-Only Shortcut
options.body: Implement a narrow Telegram config flag, accepting lower initial scope but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and cross-surface approval policy before Telegram and exec owners can implement it.
